q: By January 31, 2027 (Korea time), the joint communiqué of the 58th Security Consultative Meeting (SCM) commits to keeping U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) at 28,500 troops or at its "current level" (resolves no if no communiqué is published by then)
basis: A commitment to keep USFK at its current level appeared in the joint communiqués of the 51st SCM in 2019, the 53rd in 2021 and the 56th in 2024, but was missing from the 52nd in 2020. The 57th communiqué, in November 2025, said only that USFK "will maintain force and posture levels," without the word "current." In the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, Congress barred the Pentagon from spending money to cut USFK below 28,500 troops unless it justifies the reduction to Congress. The 2026 National Defense Strategy, by contrast, assigns South Korea primary responsibility for deterring North Korea. This year's meeting is reported likely to slip to around December over disagreements on the conditions for transferring wartime operational control (OPCON). Unlike the site's earlier forecast, which assumes a November meeting, this one asks only what the communiqué says, whenever the meeting is held, as long as the communiqué is published by January 31, 2027.
rs: The text of the 58th SCM joint communiqué, as posted by South Korea's Ministry of National Defense or the U.S. Department of Defense, in either Korean or English. It must commit to keeping USFK troops or forces at their "current level" (including wording such as "current USFK force levels") or at 28,500. Wording like the 57th communiqué's "will maintain force and posture levels," which gives neither the current level nor a number, does not count, nor does a mention of the 28,500 figure that is not a commitment.
